title: Verifier-anchored generate–validate–repair for LLM-proposed NetOps changes (preregistered, repaired)
research_question: Does integrating an LLM proposer with a formal network-change verifier (Relational NetKAT) plus a bounded model repair loop reduce the rate of verifier-failing (unsafe) configuration proposals relative to LLM generation alone?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H0: The proportion of verifier-passing proposals from the LLM+verifier+repair pipeline equals that of the unguided LLM (no improvement).
H1: The LLM+verifier+repair pipeline yields a strictly higher verifier-pass proportion than the unguided LLM within the same repair budget (falsifiable).
exploratory_questions: RQ1: Distribution of repair iterations required to reach verifier pass (0..3).
RQ2: Latency/repair-tradeoff: how much end-to-end latency is added per successful repair.

RQ3: Qualitative failure-mode taxonomy for repairs that either do not converge within 3 iterations or produce syntactically plausible but semantically incorrect fixes (captured by secondary semantic validators).
benchmark_scope: Public intent→configuration task collection assembled from public RFC examples, vendor configuration snippets, and deterministically generated synthetic topologies (all sources recorded and checksummed).
Synthetic topology instances generated deterministically with fixed RNG seeds and canonical topology templates (seeded graph generators).
Verification targets encoded as packet-trace and reachability safety properties expressible in Relational NetKAT (see doi:10.1145/3776656).
model_scope: A single hosted LLM accessible via provider API (exact model identifier will be recorded in the execution manifest).
Identical prompt templates and temperature/seed policies used for baseline and pipeline arms; repair iterations are additional model generations under the same model interface.
No local GPU execution; all model calls via hosted API (capability manifest).
transformation_scope: Prompt templates (intent→configuration) and repair-prompt templates (counterexample + instruction → revised configuration).
Deterministic canonicalization of model outputs (whitespace/token normalization) and syntactic parsing into router ACL/ACL-like ASTs before verification.
primary_estimand: Within-task paired difference in verifier-pass binary outcome: proportion_pass_pipeline − proportion_pass_baseline (primary confirmatory estimand).
secondary_estimands: Mean number of repair iterations required among tasks that eventually pass within ≤3 repairs.
Proportion of tasks fixed within k repairs for k ∈ {0,1,2,3}.
Median and 95th-percentile end-to-end latency per arm and per repair iteration.
sampling_plan: Paired design on N = 200 intent→configuration tasks that are eligible for Relational NetKAT encoding. Tasks will be drawn deterministically from public sources and seeded synthetic topology generators. Screening: automatically run a verifier-coverage test (verifier encodability and property expressibility) on candidate tasks; continue deterministic sampling up to 400 candidates until 200 eligible tasks are accepted. All sampling seeds, selection code, and provenance hashes will be published. Inclusion: tasks for which the targeted safety properties are expressible and the verifier returns a valid verdict; Exclusion: tasks failing the automated encodability test are flagged, excluded from confirmatory N, and reported with cause. Confirmatory item count = 200 (paired). Discovery items (screened candidates) cap = 400 (automated screening only).
analysis_plan: Primary test: exact paired test (McNemar exact test) on the 2×2 paired contingency (baseline vs pipeline pass/fail) to test H0 at α=0.05 (two-sided). Report exact p-value and effect-size Δ = proportion_pass_pipeline − proportion_pass_baseline with bootstrap 95% CI (10k bootstrap resamples). Secondary analyses: empirical survival curve over repair iterations (discrete-time survival), descriptive latency statistics (median, 90th, 95th), and failure-mode counts from automated semantic validators. All code, seeds, raw outputs, and analysis notebooks will be published. Sensitivity analyses: repeat primary test stratified by baseline pass probability strata and by topology size tertiles. All secondary outcomes are labelled exploratory; multiplicity adjustments described below.
multiplicity_plan: One pre-specified primary confirmatory test (McNemar) only. Secondary endpoints reported as exploratory; when reporting multiple secondary hypothesis tests, report both raw p-values and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR-adjusted p-values and clearly mark exploratory status. No alpha-spending on exploratory endpoints.
missingness_plan: Technical failures (API/network) trigger automatic deterministic retry policy: up to 2 automated retries per failed model call. If retries fail, the task is logged as 'technical failure' and the pair is excluded from the confirmatory paired test but included in a technical-failure report. If a task is excluded due to verifier-encodability discovered at screening, it does not count toward N=200 and is listed in exclusion logs with checksum and reason. No human annotation or adjudication; all exclusions are deterministic and logged.

benchmark_names: Public intent→configuration collection (public RFC/vendor snippets, synthetic seeded topologies)
risk_factors: Pre-lock development artifacts contaminating task pool or prompts
Model output caching or provider-side reuse across calls
detection_procedures: Provenance hashing: all input tasks, prompts, and selected outputs will be checksummed (SHA-256) and recorded; automated duplicate detection on hashes.
Pre-lock leakage check: cross-check checksums of samples against stored pre-lock artifact manifest; any checksum collision triggers automatic exclusion.
Model-call determinism check: log provider-returned request/response identifiers and timestamps; flag repeated identical outputs across distinct seeds/inputs for analysis.
item_flagging_rules: Automatically flag tasks whose input or prompt checksum matches any pre-lock artifact checksum.
Flag model outputs identical in byte-level content across different tasks and record for analysis (possible caching).
Flag tasks where verifier-encoding fails or returns 'unsupported property' and record as excluded.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Exclude flagged contaminated items from the confirmatory paired analysis; report exclusions and conduct sensitivity analysis including a worst-case imputation (treat excluded pipeline outcomes as failures and baseline as observed) to bound effect sizes.
residual_uncertainty: Possible verifier blindspots (false negatives) that arise from properties not expressible in Relational NetKAT; these are documented in verifier-property enumeration and counted as non-critical external-validity limitations unless they remove testability for the declared estimand.

budget_scenarios.description: Optimistic: average repairs per task = 0.5 (most initial pipeline generations pass).
models: hosted LLM API (single model; exact id logged in execution manifest)
transformations: intent→configuration prompt (1 call per arm per task)
repair prompt (0.5 average calls per task)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Baseline generation (200) + pipeline initial generation (200) + repairs (200*0.5=100) → total 500 model calls; fits well under maximum_planned_model_calls=10000 and within a short-wallclock run using hosted API with automated verifier on CPU.

models: hosted LLM API (single model; exact id logged in execution manifest)
transformations: intent→configuration prompt (1 call per arm per task)
repair prompt (1 average call per task)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Baseline generation (200) + pipeline initial generation (200) + repairs (200*1=200) → total 600 model calls. Balanced trade-off between resource cost and expected repair utility; selected as recommended because it leaves margin under 10k model-call limit and limits API cost while supporting planned analyses.

budget_scenarios.description: Pessimistic/worst-case: average repairs per task = 3.0 (repair budget exhausted often).
models: hosted LLM API (single model; exact id logged in execution manifest)
transformations: intent→configuration prompt (1 call per arm per task)
repair prompt (3 calls per task maximum)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Baseline generation (200) + pipeline initial generation (200) + repairs (200*3=600) → total 1000 model calls (explicit worst-case upper bound). Still within maximum_planned_model_calls and executable within the capability manifest, though with higher API cost and latency.

power_plan.primary_estimand: Paired difference in verifier-pass proportion (pipeline − baseline).
power_plan.target_effect: Absolute increase in pass proportion of interest for detection: approximately 0.10 (10 percentage points).
power_plan.calculation_method: Pre-registered primary test is exact McNemar paired test; effect-size reported as Δ proportion with bootstrap 95% CI. Sensitivity analyses (simulation-style) will be used to report minimum detectable effect (MDE) under a range of baseline pass rates (0.30–0.60).
assumptions: Paired independence across tasks (no repeated intents).
Screening ensures tasks are encodable by the verifier (see sampling_plan).
Two-sided α = 0.05, desired power ≈ 0.80 for primary detection target.

Baseline pass rates are uncertain; MDE depends on baseline. With N=200, the study is powered to detect approximate absolute improvements in the ~0.08–0.15 range depending on baseline and discordant-case distribution; exact MDEs will be computed and reported using pre-registered simulation scripts before data collection.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: Given paired design and N=200, detectable absolute increases (Δ) will be reported as a small table across baseline pass-rate assumptions (30%, 40%, 50%, 60%) using the pre-registered exact-McNemar simulation; we explicitly preregister that the study is primarily powered to detect Δ ≳ 0.10 under common baseline assumptions. Sensitivity analyses will be published.
sensitivity_analyses: Compute MDEs by parametric simulation across baseline pass rates (0.30,0.40,0.50,0.60) and discordant-case ratios.
Bootstrap 95% CIs for Δ with 10k resamples.
Post-hoc conditional power scan if realized discordant counts differ substantially from assumptions (reported as exploratory).

transformation_families: Intent→configuration generation (baseline and pipeline initial generation).
Canonicalization/syntax-parsing transformations (output normalization → AST) prior to verification.
semantic_equivalence_checks: Syntactic parse: automated parser that converts model text into canonical AST; outputs failing parse are automatically rejected and logged.

Deterministic verifier-equivalence checks where possible: for toy subcases, use NetKAT equivalence engine to check behavioral equivalence between model output and reference config when a reference exists.
Secondary semantic validators: automated packet-trace sandbox replay (simulator) for a prespecified set of test traces per task to detect semantically incorrect yet syntactically plausible repairs.
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject any model output that does not parse into the expected AST (automated, deterministic).
Reject outputs that cause verifier runtime errors (automated exclusion and re-prompt according to repair policy).
Reject repair outputs that introduce syntactic tokens outside the allowed configuration language grammar (automated).
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Deterministic, reproducible audit sample: 10% of passing configurations (randomly selected with fixed seed) undergo the full secondary semantic validation pipeline (packet-trace simulations) and are included in automated failure-mode classification. All audits are deterministic and reproducible; no human review.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: All prompt→input mappings use canonicalized templates and fixed RNG seeds; mapping code includes unit tests (parser round-trips) that run in CI/docker prior to execution. Mapping validation results (unit-test hashes) recorded in execution manifest.
residual_risks: Semantic correctness gaps not caught by syntactic/secondary validators (false negatives remain possible).
Verifier expressiveness limits: some operational safety properties may not be expressible in Relational NetKAT and will be excluded from the confirmatory estimand (documented list).

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: External-validity: transferability of results from public/synthetic topology instances to heterogeneous production networks remains untested (noncritical if claims are bounded to benchmark scope).

Verifier false-negative/false-positive rates on large production-scale properties: we will estimate these experimentally on held-out encodable cases but cannot guarantee coverage for properties outside Relational NetKAT expressiveness.
Operator QoE and production latency budgets are organization-specific; measured end-to-end latency in this study may not match every production tolerance (report as noncritical external limitation).
Model-provider nondeterminism or caching behaviour might vary across vendors; execution manifest will record provider metadata but reproducibility depends on provider stability.
